cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make the Test Test You
cards.instruction: Create a commitment test that gradually exposes what you are unwilling to risk yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Sign up for the overnight shift if this project matters to you. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have you signed up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'm keeping myself available for leadership decisions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: At three in the morning?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Apparently my test has reached a less comfortable definition of commitment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign up for the overnight shift if this project matters to you.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: At three in the morning?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Apparently my test has reached a less comfortable definition of commitment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give up your prize seat to prove you're on my side.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you give up yours too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine is essential for maintaining perspective.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You mean watching comfortably.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I may have designed a test I wasn't planning to take.

cards.title: Win the Smaller Concession
cards.instruction: Get one small surrender, then use its logic to make the larger claim harder to defend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Can I keep one plant on your windowsill? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One small plant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Excellent. Sunlight is available to guests. Shall we discuss the other pot?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you've agreed the principle. Now we're negotiating the size of its audience.

beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you've agreed the principle. Now we're negotiating the size of its audience.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Admit that I helped with one paragraph of the speech.

beats.text: The opening paragraph, yes.

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: Hide Inside the Callback
cards.instruction: Use an early harmless detail as the explanation for each new consequence, keeping your own role outside the pattern.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Remember the decorative ribbon? That's where the whole tent problem began. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tied it to the support rope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Yes, but nobody questioned why the ribbon was there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you pulled the rope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Following the ribbon's invitation. We should review decorative influences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.text: Remember the decorative ribbon? That's where the whole tent problem began.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tied it to the support rope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but nobody questioned why the ribbon was there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you pulled the rope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Following the ribbon's invitation. We should review decorative influences.

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Answer the Previous Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every dangerous question by sincerely answering an earlier, safer version of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. About the weather you asked earlier: yes, it rained all evening. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I asked why you crashed my car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. And before that you asked whether the roads were wet. They were.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you driving too fast?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The forecast said showers. I should answer that original question completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked if lunch was good. The soup was excellent.

cards.title: Reveal the Truth in Layers
cards.instruction: Protect someone by disclosing the truth in stages, changing what each earlier statement appears to mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The wedding venue has made a small change. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What changed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. The date remains available. The building does not.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happened to the building?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fire. Let's hold onto the available date while we choose what comes next.

beats.text: Your garden gnome is coming home in a different arrangement.
